rationale.conceptual: The paper applies well-established DFT/BTE tools to predict thermoelectric properties, requiring understanding of solid-state physics and careful convergence, but no novel algorithm development.
rationale.execution: The pipeline spans 7+ stages (relaxation, band structure, elastic constants, phonons, Born charges, third-order IFCs, ShengBTE, ZT assembly) with multiple tool handoffs and large computational tasks, demanding careful orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces a computational study of half-Heusler thermoelectrics using standard DFT and BTE tools. Conceptually, it involves careful application of established but non-trivial methods (elastic constants, phonon stability, BoltzTraP, ShengBTE). Execution is a long orchestrated pipeline with fragile handoffs between multiple specialized codes. Resource needs are moderate CPU for supercell DFT, no GPU.

compute_estimate.reasoning: CPU-bound DFT calculations on supercells (up to 4x4x4) drive the wall-clock cost; memory is modest.
